title: QuiX Quantum Commercializes Alquor 2.0 Programmable Photonic Processor Platform - Quantum Computing Report
gist: QuiX Quantum launched Alquor 2.0, a rack-mountable silicon-nitride photonic processor sold in 8/20/32-mode configurations at prices from EUR240K to EUR790K, moving boson-sampling and photonic-QIP research off free-space optical tables and into a room-temperature, data-center-ready HPC form factor; over 20 first-gen units are already deployed across academic labs.

insights.claim: QuiX Quantum has commercialized Alquor 2.0, a second-generation rack-mountable programmable photonic quantum processor built on silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuits, sold in 8-mode, 20-mode, and 32-mode configurations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Marks photonic quantum hardware's transition from lab-bench free-space optics to a standardized, purchasable rack unit, a step toward commercial productization ahead of superconducting/trapped-ion peers in some photonic niches.
insights.quote: QuiX Quantum has announced the commercial availability of Alquor 2.0, the second generation of its rack-mountable quantum photonic processor platform.

insights.claim: QuiX Quantum priced Alquor 2.0 at three tiers: EUR240,000 for the 8-mode processor, EUR490,000 for the 20-mode processor, and EUR790,000 for the 32-mode processor, with a 20% early-adopter discount on 8-mode orders from academic and public research institutions through September 30, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives investors a rare concrete price benchmark for commercial photonic quantum hardware, useful for comparing photonic processor unit economics against superconducting/trapped-ion system pricing and for tracking QuiX's revenue-per-unit trajectory.
insights.quote: QuiX Quantum has structured commercial pricing across three tiers: €240,000 for the 8-mode processor, €490,000 for the 20-mode processor, and €790,000 for the 32-mode processor.
insights.locator: QuiX Quantum has structured commercial pricing

insights.claim: Alquor 2.0 operates at room temperature (unlike superconducting qubit systems requiring dilution refrigeration) and is packaged in a 3U 19-inch chassis designed for laboratory, data center, and HPC environments, with air-cooled thermal management and a Python API for workflow automation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Room-temperature operation removes cryogenic infrastructure cost/complexity, a structural cost advantage photonic platforms can market against superconducting competitors when courting data-center and HPC customers.
insights.quote: Operating at room temperature, the system incorporates current-driver-based control electronics engineered to suppress electrical crosstalk across phase shifters, managing up to 1,000 thermo-optic modulators.
insights.locator: Alquor 2.0 integrates directly into QuiX Quantum's

themes.theme: Installed base and third-party research validation

insights.claim: QuiX Quantum has deployed over 20 first-generation Alquor units to date, which have served as testbeds for third-party academic and institutional research across multiple published arXiv papers spanning quantum walks, molecular vibronic spectra, boson sampling benchmarks, photon distillation, and search algorithms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 20+ unit installed base with a growing body of peer-reviewed/preprint publications signals genuine academic traction and a validated research ecosystem, de-risking QuiX as a hardware vendor relative to less-adopted photonic startups.
insights.quote: With over 20 first-generation units deployed to date, the Alquor platform has served as an experimental testbed for third-party academic and institutional research

insights.claim: A University of Queensland, University of Western Australia, and Pawsey Supercomputing Centre team implemented deterministic Grover search algorithms on an Alquor processor achieving 99.77% average success probability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete, high-fidelity benchmark (99.77% success) on commercially available photonic hardware gives investors a tangible performance data point to track against competing quantum search/algorithm demonstrations on other hardware platforms.
insights.quote: teams at the University of Queensland, University of Western Australia, and Pawsey Supercomputing Centre implemented deterministic Grover search algorithms with 99.77% average success probability (arXiv:2506.06435).
